Rush's younger brother, [[Brandon Rush|Brandon]], last played for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], while older brother [[JaRon Rush|JaRon]] played [[college basketball]] for [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].[https://www.nytimes.com/2008/04/07/sports/ncaabasketball/07kansas.html?ref=ncaabasketball Where Brothers Faltered, Rush Hopes to Carry On] ==College career== After graduating from [[Pembroke Hill School]] in Kansas City, Rush attended the [[University of Missouri]] in [[Columbia, Missouri]], where he was a standout guard on the basketball team. Rush averaged 19.8 points per game as a junior, leading the Tigers to the Western Regional finals in the NCAA tournament, where they lost to Oklahoma. As a sophomore in 2000–01, he led the Big 12 in scoring, averaging 21.1 points per game. During this time, Rush worked with world-renowned conditioning coach [[Istvan Javorek]]. ==Professional career== [[Image:Bonzi Wells guards Kareem Rush.jpg|thumb|left|Rush handling the ball for the Charlotte Bobcats]] ===Los Angeles Lakers (2002–2004)=== Rush entered the [[2002 NBA draft]] after his junior season and was selected with the 20th pick overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]], who immediately traded his rights to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Rush was projected to be a top 10 pick, but much like what happened to Kareem's elder brother JaRon—a former UCLA star—Kareem slipped down much further than anticipated. At the 2000 draft, JaRon, who left the Bruins after his sophomore season, was not selected. "No one wants to see something like that happen to his brother", JaRon said, weeping. "I mean, I knew he was going to get drafted eventually, but it was still hard." Over his first two seasons, he played a limited, back-up role on the [[Shaquille O'Neal]] and [[Kobe Bryant]]-led club. However, due to his three-point shooting accuracy, he would become a more frequently used reserve player in the 2003–2004 playoffs for coach [[Phil Jackson]]. Although the Lakers would lose to the Pistons in the [[2004 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Rush was able to make somewhat of a name for himself as a sharpshooter, averaging 14 minutes per game and hitting 40% of his three-point shots in the playoffs. He was a major contributor in helping the Lakers clinch the Western Conference Finals against [[Kevin Garnett]] and the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], when he scored 18 points in the sixth and final game, all from 3-point range, where he was 6 for 7.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/rushka01.html Kareem Rush Statistics - Basketball-Reference.com] ===Charlotte Bobcats (2004–2006)=== Fourteen games into the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], the Lakers traded Rush to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] for two future second-round draft picks. In Charlotte, Rush found a larger role, often starting and averaging more than 25 minutes and 11.5 points per game. He set a then-Bobcats franchise record by scoring 35 points against the [[Indiana Pacers]]. His season ended March 2 when he strained his [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] during a game in [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kareem_rush/bio.html |title=Kareem Rush Bio Page |work=NBA.com |accessdate=May 6, 2022 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515152514/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kareem_rush/bio.html |archivedate=May 15, 2013 }} ===Seattle SuperSonics (2006)=== During the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]] offseason, Rush signed with the [[Seattle SuperSonics]],[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2006/oct/04/sonics_add_extiger_rush/?mens_basketball KUsports.com - Sonics add ex-Tiger Rush] but recovered slowly from a groin injury. In November 2006, the club waived him to make room for a replacement for two frontcourt players who had sustained injuries.{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2650600 |title=Sonics sign Glyniadakis, adding depth to thin frontcourt |date=November 5, 2006 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 6, 2007 }} ===Lithuania (2006–2007)=== Rush spent the next season playing in Lithuania. On December 21, 2006, he signed with [[ULEB Cup]] participant [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos rytas]] from [[Vilnius]]. He was chosen by the Slovenian coach [[Zmago Sagadin]] and led his team to the cup final. On February 24, 2007, Rush was named [[LKL All-Star Game MVP|the MVP]] of the [[LKL All-Star Game|2007 LKL All-Star Game]]. On April 21, Rush's team became the champion of the [[Baltic Basketball League]]; he was named the Final Four [[Most valuable player|MVP]]. ===Indiana Pacers (2007–2008)=== On July 3, 2007, Rush signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]], who cited their need for a shooter.{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-pacers-rush |title=Pacers sign former first-round pick Kareem Rush |date=July 3, 2007 |access-date=July 6, 2007 |first=Cliff |last=Brunt |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101101011730/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-pacers-rush |archive-date=November 1, 2010 }} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2008–2009)=== On July 28, 2008, Rush signed a deal with the Philadelphia 76ers.{{cite news |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/hp/sports/20080728_76ers_come_to_terms_with_Kareem_Rush.html |title=76ers come to terms with Kareem Rush |first=Kate |last=Fagan |work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer|Inquirer.com]] |date=July 28, 2008 |access-date=May 6, 2022}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2009–2010)=== Rush eventually signed for the Los Angeles Clippers, because of injuries to other players on the roster.{{cite news| url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-clippers-fyi4-2009oct04,0,526630.story | work=The Los Angeles Times | title=Ready or not, let the games begin for Clippers | first=Lisa | last=Dillman | date=October 4, 2009}} However, Rush himself suffered an [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] tear in his right knee on November 18, 2009."[https://web.archive.org/web/20091203004353/http://www.google.com/hostednews/canadianpress/article/ALeqM5iDOkHBDk0KxN-Y1dLSwluxycRlGQ Clippers' G Rush tears his right ACL against the Hornets]". Associated Press. November 18, 2009. Retrieved on November 19, 2009. The day before his ACL tear would end up being his final NBA game ever. On November 17, 2009, the Clippers would lose to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] 102 - 110 with Rush only playing for less than 2 minutes and recording no stats. Rush was waived by the Clippers on January 22, 2010.{{Cite web| title = Clippers sign JamesOn Curry to 10-day contract| work = LA Times Blogs – Sports Now| access-date = February 17, 2014| date = ===Los Angeles D-Fenders (2013–2014)=== In November 2013, he was re-acquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/1314_training_camp_roster.html 2013-14 Training Camp Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610060051/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/1314_training_camp_roster.html |date=June 10, 2016 }} On January 22, 2014, Rush left the D-Fenders, citing his desire to formally retire from basketball. ===BIG3 Basketball (2017)=== In 2017, Rush joined the [[BIG3]] basketball league, playing on a talent-stacked [[3 Headed Monsters]] roster, highlighted by head coach (and [[NBA]] Hall of Famer) [[Gary Payton]], as well as [[Kwame Brown]] (the first ever directly-from-high-school player to go #1 overall in the [[NBA draft]]), [[Rashard Lewis]], [[Jason Williams (basketball, born 1975)|Jason Williams]], and [[Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf]]. === North American Premier Basketball (2018–2019)=== In January 2018, he signed with the
